# goldenpipe-native

> PyO3 binding for the goldenpipe-core planner kernel.

## What this package is

A compiled companion wheel for **goldenpipe**. You do not import it directly --
`goldenpipe` discovers it at runtime. This directory contains a compiled abi3
extension and almost no readable Python, so reading it will not tell you what it does.

## Authoritative sources

Read these instead of inferring behaviour from the binary or from the host's fallback path:

- https://docs.bensevern.dev/goldenpipe -- documentation for this surface.
- `goldenpipe/llms.txt` -- ships inside the goldenpipe wheel (`Path(goldenpipe.__file__).parent / "llms.txt"`), written for machine readers.
- https://docs.bensevern.dev/llms.txt -- index of every Golden Suite surface.
- https://github.com/benseverndev-oss/goldenmatch -- source, issues, and the decision records behind the behaviour.

## Install

```bash
pip install goldenpipe[native]   # pulls goldenpipe-native
```

## Runtime gate

- `GOLDENPIPE_NATIVE=auto` (default) -- use the kernel where it exists, fall back otherwise.
- `GOLDENPIPE_NATIVE=0` -- force the pure-Python fallback.
- `GOLDENPIPE_NATIVE=1` -- require the kernel; raise if it is missing.

Discovery lives in `goldenpipe.core._native_loader`.

## Notes

- Explicitly NOT an accelerator. The pure-Python planner is the runtime; this kernel exists so the planner can be gated against a Rust reference. Installing it does not change how your pipeline runs.

This wheel exists because a behaviour was *decided* -- which surface owns a computation,
which fallback is deliberate, which parity is contract-tested. Those decisions are
documented; the compiled artefact cannot tell you about them.
